title: Deuteronomy 31:1–8
context: Now one hundred twenty years old and barred from crossing the Jordan, Moses assures Israel that the LORD himself will go before them and that Joshua will lead. He charges the people and then Joshua, “Be strong and courageous,” because God “will not fail you nor forsake you.” The passage grounds courage in God’s presence rather than in any human leader.

verses.text: Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses goes and speaks to all Israel as his leadership nears its end. Arminian readers see a faithful servant using his final days to prepare the people for life without him.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Moses completing the ministry God gave him. The verse opens a chapter about transition, in which God provides for his people’s future beyond any single leader.

verses.text: He said to them, “I am one hundred twenty years old today. I can no more go out and come in. The LORD has said to me, ‘You shall not go over this Jordan.’
verses.arminianNotes: Moses says he is one hundred twenty years old and recalls that the LORD told him, “You shall not go over this Jordan.” Arminian readers see Moses accepting the consequence of Meribah with humility.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Moses submitting to God’s word about his own life. His honest acknowledgment of limits sets the stage for pointing Israel to God rather than to himself.

verses.text: The LORD your God himself will go over before you. He will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua will go over before you, as the LORD has spoken.
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD himself will go over before Israel, destroy the nations, and Joshua will lead. Arminian readers see God’s presence as the decisive assurance, with Joshua as his chosen instrument.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God as the true leader of the conquest, working through Joshua. The verse places God first and the human leader second, guarding against misplaced confidence.

verses.text: The LORD will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
verses.arminianNotes: God will do to the nations as he did to Sihon and Og. Arminian readers see recent victories offered as evidence that encourages trust for what lies ahead.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see past acts of God as pledges of his future faithfulness. Sihon and Og were defeated on the east side of the Jordan, as Deuteronomy 2–3 recounts.

verses.text: The LORD will deliver them up before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.
verses.arminianNotes: God will deliver the nations, and Israel must act according to all the commandment given. Arminian readers see God’s gift and Israel’s obedience held together in the conquest.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see divine deliverance calling for obedient action. The verse ties Israel’s conduct in the land to the commands already laid out in Deuteronomy.

verses.text: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them, for the LORD your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
verses.arminianNotes: Moses urges the people, “Be strong and courageous,” for God “will not fail you nor forsake you.” Arminian readers see courage grounded in God’s faithful presence rather than human strength.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s promise as the basis of confidence. Hebrews 13:5 echoes this assurance in the words “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”

verses.text: Moses called to Joshua, and said to him in the sight of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall go with this people into the land which the LORD has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.
verses.arminianNotes: Moses tells Joshua before all Israel to be strong and courageous, for he will cause them to inherit the land. Arminian readers see a public commissioning that confirms Joshua’s role to the people.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s appointed leader recognized publicly. The same charge recurs in Joshua 1:6, where God says, “Be strong and courageous; for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.”

verses.text: The LORD himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
verses.arminianNotes: Moses assures Joshua that the LORD goes before him and “will not fail you nor forsake you.” Arminian readers see personal encouragement for a leader facing an enormous task.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s presence pledged to his servant. The closing words “Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged” address the fears any new leader might feel.
